decision: Streaming TTS: progressive decode in the engine, API streaming (chunked PCM, SSE, live text input), app playback of partials, then real-engine measurements
why: task from the coordinator; DramaModel, Weights, Kernels, .metal and drama/main.swift belong to another engineer
evidence: brief

decision: Decode each step in the windows a full decode of the chunk would run (DecodeWindow.covering) instead of the last min(frames, 256 + new) frames
why: a Core ML call costs a whole 512-frame window however few frames are real, so aligned windows cost the same and reproduce the full decode exactly
evidence: Sources/DramaEngine/Codec/ProgressiveDecode.swift

decision: Under .lowLatency a chunk is never retried
why: its partials may already be playing or on the wire; a retry would repeat audio the listener heard
evidence: FrameGenerator maxRetries
result: kept; documented in help and README

decision: Keep FrameGenerator.silenceProbe beside the new codec hook
why: drama/main.swift sets silenceProbe and is not mine to edit; it should move to `codec` and the property can then go
evidence: Sources/drama/main.swift:183

decision: Seam on the Core ML codec: 600 frames (fixture codes tiled) decoded in 64-frame steps against one full decode
why: the brief's bar is 1e-3 max abs error
evidence: DRAMA_CODEC_SEAM=1 swift test --filter testSeamOnTheRealCodec
result: max abs error 0 with aligned windows; 0.0271 with a bare 256-frame context

decision: Added GenerationEstimate (time left) to the app status line, X-Drama-Estimated-Seconds and /v1/health estimate
why: coordinator's mid-task item from the user
evidence: Sources/DramaEngine/GenerationEstimate.swift; testEstimateConvergesAtASteadyRate

decision: Live route spoke the first sentence only when the third line arrived
why: splitSentences folds a short unfinished tail into the sentence before it, so the buffer never ended in a sentence mark; LiveText now cuts at the last sentence end before splitting
evidence: mock server trace: line 2 at +1 s, first audio at +5.3 s; after the fix +2.3 s

decision: curl -T - against the live route on the mock: first audio 4.0 s against 2.3 s from tools/live_speech.py with the same feed
why: curl holds piped stdin back before uploading it
evidence: scratch live_curl.sh against live_demo.sh

decision: Discarded TTFB runs 3 to 5 of the first series
why: another user's six-process Python job pushed the load average from 7 to 57 mid-series; runs 1 and 2 were clean
evidence: uptime 51.72 after the series; ps showed six python3.12 at 80 percent

decision: In-process low latency reached first audio no sooner than sentence mode (6.3 s against 7.3 s)
why: a chunk's partial waited for its final decode, and the generation thread sat in that decode before the next chunk; one serial DecodeRunner now queues the tail and the GPU moves on
evidence: StreamingBenchTests trace; commit 023f3fa

decision: Two of five low-latency runs delivered all audio at the very end
why: the end-of-run drain waited for every queued decode before emitting any; it now emits each finishing chunk as its decode lands
evidence: trace: partial 0 0..<64 at 11.25 s of an 11.25 s run; commit 477d109

decision: Decode queue at .userInteractive instead of .userInitiated
why: test whether scheduling explains the slow concurrent decode

decision: Generation speed with decode on and off: 34.9 frames/s with the codec idle while frames land, 33.0 sentence, 32.7 low latency (medians of 5); end-to-end 19.1, 15.2, 18.9 frames/s
why: the brief asks whether the CPU decode slows generation
evidence: measure rows below, mode column
result: about 6 percent slower frame rate while overlapping; no end-to-end cost

decision: First-audio limiter is the CPU decode: one window takes 1.6 s alone and about 4.6 s while the GPU generates
why: explains why low latency ties sentence mode on a 4.7 s first sentence
evidence: trace: queued at 2.50 s, audio at 7.09 s; decode-after codec_s 3.35 s for two windows
result: cause of the slowdown not isolated

decision: Kept stepFrames 64 as the default rather than 32
why: 32 starts 0.7 s sooner but every trace ran out of audio for 1.1 to 1.5 s after the first partial; 64 played without a gap in every trace
evidence: final_bench traces, low-latency and low-latency-32
